lockFileMaintenance.description: platformAutomerge stays off here: a lockfile refresh pulls versions younger than minimumReleaseAge, and GitHub's auto-merge only waits for required checks — it would merge past the pending renovate/stability-days status. Renovate-side automerge waits for its own stability check, so the 3-day age holds.

customManagers.description: The svelte-vitals-action pin that `ci install`/`ci upgrade` scaffold is a generated file nothing else refreshes (gen-action-pin.js is a manual script) — let Renovate bump it like any other dependency.

The checkout and pnpm/setup pins `ci install` scaffolds must equal this repo's workflow pins (test/ci/lockstep.test.ts), which only the built-in github-actions manager sees — extract them under the same depName and datasource so one bump moves both.

The CI guide quotes `ci install`'s output verbatim (test/ci/guide.test.ts), and the holdout workflow lives outside .github/ where the built-in github-actions manager does not look. History documents under plans/ and docs/superpowers/ keep their old pins on purpose, so they are not listed.

packageRules.description: Auto-merge everything except major updates (those need review) — CI still has to pass first. The Renovate app is on main's ruleset bypass list specifically so these can merge without a human review.

Later rules win: a pin bump changes what `ci install` scaffolds, so it needs a changeset before it can ship — no automerge, a human adds one. No release-age wait either: the action is first-party, and until the pin moves the scaffolded CI analyzes with an older core than the CLI.

Later rules win: these bumps also change what `ci install` scaffolds and the English CI guide, so a human adds the changeset and re-stamps the guide's translation (blume translate --check) before merge.
Published packages' engines.node is a public compatibility floor for consumers, not a dev-toolchain pin — never auto-bump it.
@types/node follows the published engines.node floor (Node 24), not the dev runtime: newer typings would let code type-check against APIs the floor does not have.
matchUpdateTypes keeps this rule off the lockFileMaintenance update type — without it, the group rename splits lock file maintenance into a second, permanently-conflicting -catalog twin PR.
The default catalog stays on SvelteKit 2, which most analyzed apps still use; SvelteKit 3 lives in the kit3 catalog, used only by examples/sveltekit-3.
adapter-static 4 requires SvelteKit 3, so it is held with it.
